title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: PMET workforce and EA coverage
sections.summary: 54% of resident workforce are PMETs and 34% PMEs, and PMEs earning over $4,500 monthly are not covered under the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Today, 54% of our resident workforce are professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) and 34% are professionals, managers and executives (PMEs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: There have been many PMEs approaching the Labour Movement for help via our various workplace advisory platforms with a variety of issues from unfair dismissals to breaches of provisions in the Employment Act (EA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, PMEs with a monthly basic salary of more than $4,500 are not covered under the Act.

sections.label: Three proposed EA changes
sections.summary: Proposes expanding EA scope to cover PMEs beyond $4,500, extending Part IV protection beyond $2,500, and enhancing dispute resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, expansion of the scope of EA to cover PMEs beyond the current $4,500 limit; second, extension of the Part IV protection to cover non-workmen beyond the current $2,500 limit; and third, enhancements to the existing dispute resolution framework.

sections.label: Removing $4,500 salary cap
sections.summary: Questions the PME versus Rank and File dichotomy and proposes removing the $4,500 salary cap so all employees get EA protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, whether there is a need to have this "PME versus Rank and File" dichotomy is something we need to review whether now or in the near future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I submit, therefore, we should remove this $4,500 salary cap completely so that all employees in Singapore can enjoy the basic protection under EA.

sections.label: Reviewing salary limits
sections.summary: Submits that the $2,500 and $4,500 limits need review and raising to keep pace with rising median wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: To keep pace with wage movements, I submit there is a need to review both the $2,500 and $4,500 limits accordingly and raise it to keep pace with rising median wages.

sections.label: Section 18A employee transfers
sections.summary: Section 18A allows for the transfer of employees to a new entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Section 18A allows for the transfer of employees to a new entity.

sections.label: Three EA review areas
sections.summary: Lists removing the salary ceiling, raising the Part 4 non-manual workers cap, and enhancing dispute mediation, noting PMEs earning $4,500 or more lack EA protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First of all, we should remove the salary ceiling to cover all workers, including PMEs with monthly salary exceeding $4,500, so that they will all be protected under EA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, with the rise in median salary, the monthly salary cap of non-manual workers covered under Part 4 of the EA should also increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, the current dispute mediation framework should also be enhanced, for example, to allow the ECT to handle unfair dismissal cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: (In English): In summary, these three areas are important areas for review to ensure the EA stays relevant and serves the needs of the future workforce, the future of work and the future of workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, we must bear in mind that the amendments should not compromise the need to preserve effective collective bargaining and bring more workers within the tripartite relationship.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, currently, PMEs who earn a basic salary of $4,500 or more are not protected under the EA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to recent employment data, the median gross salary of resident employees is about $4,050 a month.

sections.label: Term contract workers share
sections.summary: Term contract workers make up 10% of the resident workforce.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, term contract workers make up 10% of our resident workforce.

sections.label: Standard adoption by employers
sections.summary: Minister Josephine Teo said 400 employers adopted the Standard, covering over 28,000 resident term contract workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: When I asked the Parliamentary Question (PQ) on the compliance mechanisms for the Standard in October last year, Minister Josephine Teo said that in two months, 400 employers, accounting for more than 28,000, or 17%, of all resident term contract workers, have adopted the Standard.

sections.label: Missing retrenchment benefits recommendation
sections.summary: The Standard lacks a retrenchment benefits recommendation, and three vulnerable groups are covered: women, foreign domestic workers and people with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The notice period is the same as the notice period for retrenchment of permanent employees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But what is missing in the Standard for Term Contract Workers is the recommendation of retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Without this recommendation in the Standard, term contracts remain a risk of being the route for employers to avoid the moral and regulatory pressure of retrenching employees responsibly and fairly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are three groups of vulnerable employees I will cover in this cut: women, foreign domestic workers (FDWs) and people with disabilities.

sections.label: Protecting women from harassment
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to consider two ways of enhancing protection of women from workplace harassment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider two ways of enhancing protection of women from workplace harassment?

sections.label: Empowering bodies on harassment
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to consider empowering TGFEP or two other bodies on workplace harassment grievances, or extending its hotline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider empowering either TGFEP or the other two bodies to deal with workplace harassment grievances, or have its hotline for reporting labour infringements be extended specifically to workplace harassment as well?

sections.label: Replacing should with must
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to replace "should" with "must" in the guide where appropriate for domestic workers' safety and rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But if we believe in workers' safety and workers' rights, then surely our domestic workers must sleep in safe quarters and must mutually agree on their rest days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, can the Ministry replace "should" with "must" in the guide wherever appropriate?

sections.label: Unfair dismissal definition and remedies
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry can amend the EA to define unfair dismissal more clearly and set out legal remedies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry amend the EA to provide a clearer definition of what constitutes an "unfair" dismissal and set out legal remedies for unfair dismissals?

sections.label: Singapore economy and employment 2017
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's economy grew 3.6% in 2017 and that a drop in total employment was reported.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Singapore economy grew by 3.6% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On the employment front, we were informed of a drop in Singapore's total employment in 2017.

sections.label: Productivity growth and labour limits
sections.summary: The passage states tripartite partners restructured business processes and the workforce, with 3% productivity growth that some economists say may not be sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The tripartite partners have restructured business processes and the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We achieved 3% productivity growth last year but some economists have cautioned that such a pace might not be sustainable because of limits from a tight labour market.

sections.label: Manpower shortage and Industry Transformation Maps
sections.summary: The passage asks MOM's assessment of manpower shortage problems given 23 Industry Transformation Maps and needed new skills and talents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Given that we are rolling out 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), and new skills and talents are needed to make these transformations successful, what is MOM's assessment of the manpower shortage problems?

sections.label: Foreign workers quality and FCF
sections.summary: The passage asks what is being done to raise foreign workers' quality, noting foreigners are a third of the workforce and citing the FCF and National Jobs Bank.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With a third of our workforce comprising of foreigners, what is being done to raise the quality of foreign workers in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: It has been an arduous but positive journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: We have seen the introduction of the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) and the National Jobs Bank in 2014.

sections.label: FCF effectiveness and nationality bias
sections.summary: The passage asks MOM for an update on FCF's effectiveness in levelling the playing field for local PMEs and eradicating nationality bias in hiring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: In this regard, I wish to ask MOM to provide an update on how effective FCF has been in the past three years since implementation in levelling the playing field for our local PMEs and in eradicating "nationality bias" discrimination in hiring practices, including by employment and placement agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I know the Minister has shared that he has nailed more than 300 companies into what he calls the "watchlist" where he sees the "Triple Weak".

sections.label: Jobs Bank advertising exemptions
sections.summary: Lists four cases where companies are exempted from the Jobs Bank advertising requirement, including small firms and high-salary or short-term jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Suggestion 1 – At present, you are exempted from the Jobs Bank advertising requirement in any of these cases: (a) your company has 25 or fewer employees; (b) the job position is paying a fixed monthly salary of $12,000 and above; (c) the job is to be filled by an intra-corporate transferee (ICT); and (d) the job is necessary for short-term contingencies, that is, the period of employment in Singapore is not more than one month.

sections.label: Procurement from Triple Weak companies
sections.summary: Suggests companies and the public sector avoid buying from Triple Weak companies or instead buy from HCP-recognised ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Suggestion 3 – To encourage building a strong Singaporean Core, companies and organisations which outsource some of their services, such as information technology (IT), HR or accounting and even construction projects, can, within the terms of the tender or contract, not buy from these Triple weak companies, or purchase from companies or organisations which have been recognised by the HCP mark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I suggest the public sector, including Government-linked corporations, take the lead and should not procure services or buy from any of these Triple Weak companies.

sections.label: Singapore ease of doing business rank
sections.summary: States that a World Bank report last year ranked Singapore second in the world for ease of doing business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: According to a World Bank report last year, Singapore ranked second in the world for ease of doing business.

sections.label: FCF Watchlist company count
sections.summary: States that during last year's COS debate, MOM shared there were 250 companies on the FCF Watchlist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Last year, during the COS debate, MOM shared that there were 250 companies on the FCF Watchlist.

sections.label: FCF Watchlist rise to 300
sections.summary: States that in October 2017 MOM shared the FCF Watchlist rose to 300 companies, which the speaker calls unsatisfactory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In October 2017, MOM shared that the number of such companies on the FCF Watchlist has gone up to 300 companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This is clearly unsatisfactory as it suggests that these companies are not deterred by the punitive action by MOM and are also not bothered about creating more employment for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Subvention update and PME benefit
sections.summary: Asks for an update on the subvention's success and benefit to local PMEs, citing feedback that it may not suffice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I wish to ask for an update and how successful it has been thus far and how does it benefit our local PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I have received feedback from the professional services industry, including the information and communications technology (ICT) and financial sectors, that the current subvention may not suffice and appear unattractive, considering the wage levels of experts in these sectors.

sections.label: CTP grants outcomes and metrics
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to elaborate on expected CTP grant outcomes and metrics, warning CTP should not lighten companies' routine training costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this light, can the Minister elaborate on the outcomes expected from CTP grants and the metrics that would be used to measure the outcomes to make sure the money is well spent?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am asking this because we have to be careful that CTP is not used to lighten the costs incurred by companies for routine training for their workers.

sections.label: CTP company-level project examples
sections.summary: The passage asks for examples of company-level CTP-funded projects and how capability transferred benefits the whole sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister give some examples of company-level projects funded by CTP and how the scenario I just described was avoided?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How has the Ministry ensured the capability transferred to a company would benefit the sector as a whole?

sections.label: Number of self-employed persons
sections.summary: The passage states that the number of self-employed persons has reached 200,000 to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To date, the number of self-employed persons has already reached 200,000.

sections.label: Labour shortages in certain sectors
sections.summary: The passage states there are substantial labour shortages in sectors such as healthcare and in occupational jobs such as skilled technicians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Unfortunately, there are substantial labour shortages in certain sectors, such as in healthcare and occupational jobs, such as skilled technicians.

sections.label: Lean Enterprise Development Scheme launch
sections.summary: The passage states LEDS was launched in 2015 to grow a manpower-lean workforce, build a strong Singaporean Core and nurture a higher-quality workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: The Lean Enterprise Development Scheme (LEDS) was launched in 2015 to grow a more manpower-lean workforce, help build a strong Singaporean Core and nurture a higher-quality workforce.

sections.label: LEDS effectiveness for companies
sections.summary: The passage asks how effective LEDS has been in helping companies transform and become manpower-lean, noting over 5,000 companies tapped it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how effective LEDS has been in helping companies transform and become more manpower-lean?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: It has been reported that over 5,000 companies have tapped on LEDS to transform their business operations and improve productivity.

sections.label: Citizen unemployment and work schemes
sections.summary: Citizen unemployment rose to about 3.3% in 2017, and it asks whether schemes like Work Trial and Career Trial can cover all worker groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Our citizen unemployment has crept to about 3.3% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Can the various schemes, including the Work Trial and Career Trial, be further expanded to cover all groups of workers?

sections.label: Long-term resident unemployment rise
sections.summary: Long-term unemployment hit a 14-year high in 2016, with 17,600 workers jobless at least 25 weeks and a 0.8% long-term resident rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: Long-term unemployment rose to its highest in 14 years in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: In September 2016, three in 10 unemployed resident workers could not find employment after more than six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: The long-term resident unemployment rate rose to 0.8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: This meant that 17,600 workers were jobless for at least 25 weeks.

sections.label: PCP placements of PMETs
sections.summary: PCP placed 3,300 PMETs in 2017, but only 10% were long-term unemployed workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: PCP placed 3,300 PMETs in 2017, but only 10% were long-term unemployed workers.

sections.label: Self-employed persons share and preference
sections.summary: The TWG Report says SEPs are 8% to 10% of the resident workforce, and 80% prefer self-employment mainly for autonomy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, based on the TWG Report on self-employed persons (SEPs), the share of SEPs is at 8% to 10% of our total resident workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: The report had also indicated that the majority of SEPs – 80% of them – prefer self-employment over regular employment, primarily for the autonomy.

sections.label: Challenges facing self-employed persons
sections.summary: SEPs may earn more but face irregular income, no training and development framework, and no health and income protection for prolonged illness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Although SEPs have the potential to earn a higher income, they do face irregular income streams, lack of a framework for training and development and do not have health and income protection to manage prolonged or sudden illnesses.

sections.label: Graduate and MOM freelance surveys
sections.summary: A joint NUS, NTU and SMU survey shows freelance work rose to 2.4% in 2017, and an MOM 2016 survey found 83% of about 200,000 respondents preferred freelance work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the recent joint graduate employment survey of graduates from the National University of Singapore (NUS), Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and Singapore Management University (SMU), results state that more went into freelance work – 2.4% in 2017 compared to 1.7% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In another survey conducted by MOM in 2016, 83% of approximately 200,000 respondents cited freelance work as their preferred choice of employment.

sections.label: MediSave contributions for gig workers
sections.summary: The Ministry accepts a contribute-as-you-earn MediSave model for self-employed persons, and the speaker asks about further incentives for voluntary CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry has indicated it accepts the TWG's recommendation of a contribute-as-you-earn model for MediSave whereby contributions to the SEP's MediSave account of CPF is required as and when a service fee is earned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the Ministry further studies its implementation, could the Government also look into more ways to encourage gig workers to make further voluntary contributions to their CPF by providing them with strong incentives to do so?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, could a "default" be established where CPF deductions, beyond MediSave, initially match those of regular-economy workers with the same job profile but, being non-binding, would permit opting into a lower amount?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Alternatively, could gig workers receive information in their CPF statements about typical contributions by regular-economy workers in comparable employment circumstances, to encourage them to follow the "social norm"?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Government look into offering incentives for SEPs who voluntarily contribute to their Ordinary, Special or Retirement accounts, including favourable tax treatment when they do so?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in 2017, the labour force participation rate for women aged 15 and above was 59.8%.

sections.label: Gender by monthly income brackets
sections.summary: More women than men are employed only in jobs paying under $1,500 monthly, while men outnumber women in every bracket from $1,500 to below $11,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: The only income brackets where there are more women employees than men are jobs where the monthly salaries are less than $1,500.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: For jobs that pay a monthly salary of at least $1,500 up to below $11,000, there are consistently more male employees than female employees in every income bracket.

sections.label: Protections for pregnant employees
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry can give employees the right to return to their job and prohibit termination during pregnancy, maternity leave and three months after.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry enhance protections for mothers by giving employees the right to return to their job and prohibit any termination during an employee's pregnancy, maternity leave, as well as three months after returning to work from her maternity leave?

sections.label: Legislated right to request FWAs
sections.summary: The speaker encourages the Ministry to consider giving parents of newly born children a legislated right to request flexible work arrangements in the child's first year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Frequently, the inertia of established work processes and schedules causes employers to go beyond part-time work as an FWA option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: I would encourage the Ministry to consider giving to our young parents with newly born children the legislated right to request for FWAs in the first year of birth of their children.

sections.label: Fair Employment Practices pledge adoption
sections.summary: 5,219 unique companies have pledged on Fair Employment Practices, but only 11.8% have adopted these standards to date.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
sentences.text: While 5,219 unique companies have pledged on Fair Employment Practices, only 11.8% have adopted these standards to date.

sections.label: Workplace harassment advisory promotion
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Ministry can intensify promotion of the Tripartite Advisory standards, including a public database of employers with written harassment policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
sentences.text: MOM can work with human capital partners, tertiary institutions, trade unions and grassroots organisations to spread the stringent qualifying criteria to be a TS Adopter, and to educate the public on its importance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: However, the Ministry does not track how many employers have implemented the Tripartite Advisory on managing workplace harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The Association of Women for Action and Research's (AWARE's) Sexual Assault Care Centre saw 108 cases of workplace-related incidents in 2017, a rise from 91 cases in 2016 and 66 cases in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: This suggests workplace harassment is a common problem that employees are increasingly voicing out against.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can the Ministry intensify promotion of the Advisory standards to employers, including setting up and maintaining a public database for employers to voluntarily declare that they have written policies to manage workplace harassment?

sections.label: Workplace harassment complaint figures
sections.summary: TAFEP received 800 complaints in three years with fewer than five on workplace harassment, contrasting with AWARE survey figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Lim Swee Say told the House last year that TAFEP received 800 complaints over the last three years, of which fewer than five were about workplace harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was not clear if these included sexual harassment cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This contrasted with the survey done by AWARE in 2008 with 500 respondents where 54% of the respondents experienced sexual harassment at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But more recently, according to a Straits Times report on 10 December 2017, one in four cases at AWARE's Sexual Assault Care Centre are about workplace harassment.

sections.label: CPF members meeting Basic Retirement Sum
sections.summary: Minister Teo said that in 2016, 58% of active CPF members at age 55 met the Basic Retirement Sum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Chairman, just last month, Minister Teo shared in this House that in 2016, 58% of active CPF members at age 55 met the Basic Retirement Sum.

sections.label: Workfare recipients below retirement sum
sections.summary: Of the remaining 42% without enough for the Basic Retirement Sum, 55% were Workfare Income Supplement recipients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Among the remaining 42% who have not accumulated enough for the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS), 55% were Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme recipients.

sections.label: Flat type and Silver Support payouts
sections.summary: HDB flat type is not part of means-testing, but seniors in larger flats get less payouts though equally needy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: The HDB flat type is not part of the means-testing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: However, seniors who live in larger flats get less payouts though they are just as needy as those who live in smaller flats.

sections.label: Questions on Silver Support Scheme
sections.summary: Questions ask the rationale for tiered payouts, gender breakdown of beneficiaries, and how many lost eligibility and why.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Can the Minister explain the rationale behind the tiered payouts?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: What is the breakdown of beneficiaries of the Silver Support Scheme by gender?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Since the payouts started, how many beneficiaries have lost their eligibility for Silver Support and what were the reasons?

sections.label: Gender differentiated CPF Life premiums
sections.summary: Gender differentiated premiums for CPF Life compound the effect of the gender income gap.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, the gender differentiated premiums for CPF Life compounds the effect of the gender income gap.

sections.label: Older family caregivers study
sections.summary: A 2017 CARE study found caregivers above 70 are mainly female spouses, many in declining health, giving up to 60 hours weekly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: The 2017 study on Singapore's older family caregivers by CARE showed that caregivers above 70 years old are primarily spouses, 90% of whom are female.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Many of them are in declining health themselves, with 30% showing symptoms of clinical depression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Despite their frailty, they dedicate up to 60 hours a week in caregiving.

sections.label: Tax rebates and caregiver allowances
sections.summary: Proposed help includes tax rebates for families with caregiver members and direct allowances with CPF contributions for caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: To help them, one way is to provide tax rebates for families who have members who are caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Another would be through direct allowances, with CPF contributions provided to caregivers to defray the loss of incomes due to caregiving and ensure long-term security.

sections.label: Older workers re-entry rate
sections.summary: Long-term unemployment rose 0.02% from 2015 to 2017, but under 56% of workers aged 50 and above re-entered, below the 66% national average.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: While the number of long-term unemployed has risen only 0.02% for the period 2015 to 2017, what is worrying is the re-entry rate of older workers aged 50 and above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: It was found that less than 56% of resident workers aged 50 or older were able to re-enter the job market, compared to more than 66% for the national average.

sections.label: CPF rates above 55
sections.summary: Above age 55, employee CPF contribution is cut by 7% and employer by 4%, an 11% combined monthly reduction.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: At the moment, once employees are more than 55 years old, the employee CPF contribution is reduced by 7% while the employer CPF contribution is reduced by 4%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: This results in an overall reduction of 11% for their combined CPF contribution each month.

sections.label: Proposed CPF contribution rates
sections.summary: The passage proposes keeping employer CPF contribution at 17% and employee CPF contribution at 20%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Let it remain at 17% for employer CPF contribution at 20% for employee CPF contribution.

sections.label: WorkPro Job Redesign Grant
sections.summary: The Ministry enhanced the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant in July 2016; over 600 companies applied, benefiting over 9,500 older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: The Ministry had enhanced the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant in July 2016 to encourage companies to redesign jobs for our senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: More than 600 companies had applied for the grant to date, benefiting over 9,500 older workers.

sections.label: PCPs help mid-career individuals
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance said in his Budget Statement that PCPs helped more than 3,700 mid-career individuals take up new jobs last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance mentioned in his Budget Statement that the PCPs have helped more than 3,700 mid-career individuals take up new jobs last year.

sections.label: Seniors stonewalled by employers
sections.summary: The speaker has met seniors interested in working who find themselves stonewalled after employers learn their age despite relevant experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In the course of my community work, I have met a good number of seniors who have expressed interest in working and, yet, despite relevant experience, find themselves stonewalled after employers find out about their age.

sections.label: Job Redesign for Older Workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Job Redesign for Older Workers could be identified as a key component of each ITM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao
sentences.text: Could we expressly identify Job Redesign for Older Workers as a key component of each ITM to be set out among the suite of initiatives for improving productivity in any given industry, so that we may spur the collective thinking that can go into finding better solutions of Job Redesign for Older Workers, and direct some of the industry’s efforts at innovation in this direction?

sections.label: Racial discrimination in housing and employment
sections.summary: Surveys and personal accounts indicate racial discrimination remains prevalent in housing and employment, with One Singapore survey respondents reporting job application discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Surveys conducted over the years continue to indicate that racial discrimination remains an issue in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These surveys, coupled with personal accounts, showed that racial discrimination is prevalent, specifically in the areas of housing and employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, in the recent survey conducted by One Singapore, 48% of the Malay respondents and 41% of the Indian respondents and respondents of other ethnicities said that they face discrimination when applying for a job.

sections.label: Racism and racial discrimination convention
sections.summary: The speaker says people often do not consciously try to be racist, and notes Singapore ratified the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination in November last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: People often do not consciously try to be racist even when the actions actively marginalised others or, at least, make others feel uncomfortable or unwelcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I also understand that Singapore has recently ratified the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination in November last year.

sections.label: Discrimination on basis of mental illness
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister how many cases of discrimination on the basis of mental illness were reported to MOM and the investigation outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Can the Minister please share how many cases of discrimination on the basis of mental illness have been reported to MOM and the outcomes of the investigations by MOM?

sections.label: Cleaning and security PWM wage increases
sections.summary: The cleaning and security PWMs were enhanced to give year-on-year wage increments, partly addressing down-waging at contract renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: The cleaning and security PWMs were recently enhanced to provide these workers with year-on-year increments in wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: These planned built-in increases in wages will partly address the problem of "down-waging" when their contracts are being renewed.

sections.label: Compulsory rest areas for outsourced workers
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a review of WSH guidelines to make designated rest areas compulsory for outsourced workers at their workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: These workers deserve the proper dignity of having proper rest areas so that they can carry out their work more productively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to call for a review of the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) guidelines to incorporate compulsory designated rest areas for outsourced workers, such as cleaners, landscape workers and security guards, at their respective workplaces.

sections.label: WSH representative for BizSAFE Level 3
sections.summary: The speaker suggests making it compulsory for companies to appoint a WSH representative as part of BizSAFE Level 3 certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While we ponder over this, perhaps a more practical approach would be to make it compulsory for companies to appoint a WSH representative as part of the certification for BizSAFE Level 3.

sections.label: Return-To-Work Programme launch
sections.summary: The speaker had highlighted the need for a support framework beyond WICA, and the tripartite partners launched the Return-To-Work Programme in November 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At last year’s COS debate, I highlighted the need for a support framework, beyond the existing Workplace Injury Compensation Act (WICA), to help our injured workers return to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the tripartite partners launched the Return-To-Work (RTW) Programme in November 2017.

sections.label: Mandatory reporting of workplace harassment
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Minister to make reporting of workplace abuse and harassment mandatory, treating such harm like work-related accident injury.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
sentences.text: For a start, an injury or harm as a result of workplace harassment must be treated with the same level of priority as an injury from a work-related accident.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to make the reporting of workplace abuse and harassment mandatory.

sections.label: Mediation body for harassment cases
sections.summary: The speaker proposes forming a mediation body because POHA remedies may not address individual concerns efficiently and cost-effectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
sentences.text: Under the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA), even though a range of civil remedies and criminal sanctions is available to better protect people from harassment and related anti-social behaviour, it may not be sufficient to address individual concerns efficiently and cost effectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
sentences.text: Therefore, I propose to form a mediation body to address such cases efficiently and in a cost-effective manner.

sections.label: Act enhancement against cyber threats
sections.summary: The Act needs enhancement to protect employees from workplace abuse and cyber realm attacks, with measures to deter physical abuse and protect cyberspace from unfounded attacks.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
sentences.text: The Act needs to be enhanced to address such threats and to protect employees from not just workplace abuse, but from the cyber realm as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
sentences.text: As we put in measures to deter potential physical abuse, we must also look at measures to protect the cyberspace from unfounded attacks.

sections.label: Foreign labour abuse reports
sections.summary: Reports describe foreign labour abuse including overcrowded dormitories, expired food and underpaid salaries, with workers raising money for recruitment agencies making them vulnerable to forced labour and debt bondage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Over the last year, there have been reports of appalling cases of foreign labour abuse, from over-crowded, unsanitary dormitories, to workers served expired food, to workers forced to accept less than half their promised salaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: In order to come to Singapore to work, many foreign workers have to raise significant sums of money to pay recruitment agencies, making them vulnerable to forced labour and debt bondage.

sections.label: Job advertising on Jobs Bank
sections.summary: Employers must advertise job vacancies on the online Jobs Bank before submitting EP applications, ensuring Singaporeans are considered fairly for openings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Currently, based on our FCF before the submission of any EP applications, employers are required to advertise the job vacancies on the online Jobs Bank so that there are measures to ensure Singaporeans are considered fairly for these openings.

sections.label: Foreign workers' in-principle approval
sections.summary: Foreign workers accept work in Singapore based on their in-principle approval, which lists their jobs, pay and deductions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: At the moment, foreign workers accept work in Singapore based on their in-principle approval (IPA) which lists their jobs, pay and deductions.

sections.label: Standardised contract before Work Permits
sections.summary: MOM should mandate a standardised contract signed by both parties and submitted to MOM before Work Permits can be issued as a basic fair employment practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: As a basic fair employment practice, MOM should mandate that a standardised contract be issued and signed by both parties and submitted to MOM before Work Permits can be issued.

sections.label: Mandatory bank salary payments
sections.summary: Salary vouchers are easily forged and disputed, so MOM is asked to consider mandatory bank payments for non-domestic workers, as Gulf states have implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The only documentation that payments have been made is salary vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: However, salary vouchers are easily forged and might not tally with the cash amount paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: When workers lodge complaints and salary vouchers are disputed, it is very difficult for MOM to ascertain where the truth lies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Will MOM consider making it mandatory to pay salaries to non-domestic workers through banks, creating an audit trail as to how much was actually paid?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Many states in the Gulf ‒ the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Oman ‒ have also implemented such a mandatory requirement.

sections.label: Job growth and unemployment
sections.summary: Net job growth slowed from over 100,000 a year to under 10,000 a year, and the resident unemployment rate rose to 3.2% in December 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Net job growth slowed from more than 100,000 a year to less than 10,000 a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The resident unemployment rate increased to 3.2% in December 2016.

sections.label: Manpower growth and productivity
sections.summary: Over the past three years manpower growth slowed from an average of 4% to 1%, while productivity gain grew from 0.4% to 1.8% per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In the past three years, manpower growth has slowed from an average of 4% to 1%, while productivity gain has grown from 0.4% previously to 1.8% over the last three years on average, 1.8% per year over the last three years.

sections.label: Needed net job growth
sections.summary: Average net job growth of under 10,000 a year was not high enough and needs to rise to about 25,000 to 40,000 a year for a 3.4 million workforce growing at about 1%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Average net job growth of less than 10,000 a year in the past three years was not high enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We need to bring it up to about 25,000 to 40,000 a year to provide enough jobs for a 3.4 million workforce growing at about 1%.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow jobseekers
sections.summary: Last year, under the Adapt and Grow initiative, more than 25,000 jobseekers were helped to secure jobs successfully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Last year, under the Adapt and Grow initiative, we helped more than 25,000 jobseekers to secure jobs successfully.

sections.label: Removing EA salary cap
sections.summary: The salary cap of the Employment Act will be removed to cover all employees, including all PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: First, we will remove the salary cap of EA to cover all employees, including all PMETs.

sections.label: Extending EA benefits to employees
sections.summary: All core employee benefits and protections in the Employment Act will be extended to all employees, covering an additional 430,000 PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: All core employee benefits in EA, including annual leave, paid public holidays, paid sick leave and paid hospitalisation leave and other protection, such as timely payment of salary, maternity protection and childcare leave, statutory protection against wrongful dismissal and the right to preserve existing terms and conditions for employment transfer resulting from sale of business and business restructuring, all these will now be extended to all employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: And this will cover an additional 430,000 PMEs.

sections.label: Salary caps for workmen and non-workmen
sections.summary: The $4,500 workmen salary cap covers over 99% of workmen, while the non-workmen cap rises from $2,500 to $2,600, covering half the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For workmen, the current salary cap of $4,500 already covers more than 99% of workmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: But for non-workmen, the current cap of $2,500 will be raised to $2,600 so that this enhancement will extend coverage to half of our workforce.

sections.label: Shift to ECT one-stop service
sections.summary: The shift to ECT will give employers and employees one-stop service, with amendments to EA to be tabled this year for implementation by 1 April next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We will shift it over to ECT to provide both employers and employees with "one-stop service".

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We will seek Parliament's approval of these amendments to EA later this year for implementation by 1 April next year.

sections.label: EP applications withheld or rejected
sections.summary: Since February 2016, 1,900 EP applications have been withheld or rejected by MOM or withdrawn by companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Since we started in February 2016, a total of 1,900 EP applications have been withheld or rejected by MOM or withdrawn by the companies.

sections.label: Singaporean PMETs hired by companies
sections.summary: More than 2,200 Singaporean PMETs were hired by these companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: As a result, more than 2,200 Singaporean PMETs were hired by these companies.

sections.label: Watchlist companies and work pass privileges
sections.summary: 150 of 500 companies exited the Watchlist; 60 of the remaining 350 were uncooperative, so their work pass privileges were curtailed until they adopt fair HR practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: After being removed from the Watchlist, the company continues to hire and develop more of our local wealth managers and PMETs to grow their business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So far, 150 companies out of the 500 companies have improved their HR practices and exited from the Watchlist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Of the remaining 350 companies, 60 of them have not been cooperative and showed no signs of improvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We have curtailed their work pass privileges: no new EP applications, no renewal of existing EPs, until they adopt fair HR practices.

sections.label: Expanding Jobs Bank advertising requirement
sections.summary: The FCF will be strengthened by expanding the Jobs Bank advertising requirement before EP application to employers with at least 10 employees, not just over 25.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: To ensure fair access to more jobs and better jobs, we will strengthen the FCF further, as suggested by Mr Patrick Tay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We will expand the requirement to advertise jobs on the national Jobs Bank before EP application to cover more employers, not just those with more than 25 employees, but also those with at least 10 employees.

sections.label: Entry level salary increase
sections.summary: Entry level salary rises by $200, from $2,200 to $2,400, in two $100 steps from January next year and January 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: I agree with Mr Patrick Tay that it is timely to review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We will increase entry level salary by $200, up from $2,200 to $2,400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: To allow companies more time to adjust, the increase will be done in two steps: $100 from January next year and the next $100 from January 2020.

sections.label: Maximum employment period extension
sections.summary: Maximum employment period is extended by four years, from 18 to 22 and 22 to 26, for all sectors and R1 and R2 from 1 May this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In response to feedback from the industry, we will extend the maximum period of employment by another four years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Those on 18 years, to 22 years; and from 22 years to 26 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This will apply to all sectors and for both R1 and R2 to take effect from 1 May this year.

sections.label: HC Partners on board
sections.summary: One hundred and thirty-four HC Partners are now on board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: One hundred and thirty-four HC Partners are now on board.

sections.label: Jimmy Wong sales and synergy
sections.summary: Mr Jimmy Wong went from delivery driver to Sales Executive, bringing $1 million in sales in six months, and synergy between two-thirds local and one-third foreign must be strengthened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Starting off as a delivery driver, Mr Jimmy Wong is now a Sales Executive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: He brought in $1 million worth of sales in just six months in his new job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The company was able to attract 20% more job applications last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: But what is even more impressive is that 100% of those they offered jobs to accepted their offers!

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Fifth and last, we must strengthen the synergy between "two-thirds local" and "one-third foreign" so that the outcome will not be "equal to one", but "greater than one".

sections.label: Predictive management and AI Singapore
sections.summary: Adopting predictive management means near-zero operation incidents, and AI Singapore anchors deep national capabilities in AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The adoption of predictive management will mean near-zero operation incidents, such as no machine breakdowns, no product defects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We now have AI Singapore, our National AI programme, to anchor deep national capabilities in AI.

sections.label: Pharmaceutical cargo IATA certification
sections.summary: Over 20,000 tonnes of global pharmaceutical cargo pass through Changi Airport annually, and the aim is up to 25 IATA-certified companies, up from 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In the area of pharmaceutical transportation, today, more than 20,000 tonnes of global pharmaceutical cargo go through Changi Airport annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The global market is still growing and growing very fast.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: But out of 209 companies certified by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) to handle such cargo, we have only 10 of them here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In total, we aim for up to 25 companies, up from the 10 currently to 25, to be able to obtain IATA certification.

sections.label: Local furnishing industry size
sections.summary: The local furnishing industry is a S$6 billion industry with over 1,900 companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Not many of us know that our local furnishing industry is a S$6 billion industry with over 1,900 companies.

sections.label: Funding support for capability transfer
sections.summary: Funding support ranges from 30%, 50% and 70% of capability transfer cost, including trainers' salaries, allowances, airfare and training equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Funding support will range from 30%, 50% and 70% of the cost of capability transfer, which includes the salary cost of the expert trainers, both local and foreign; cost of living allowances in Singapore and overseas; airfare and training equipment for the industry.

sections.label: Exceptional case funding support
sections.summary: In exceptional cases with high capability transfer cost and lacking local expertise, up to 90% funding and projects over $300,000 are assessed case-by-case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In exceptional cases, as highlighted by Mr Patrick Tay, where the cost of capability transfer is high, and local expertise is much needed but lacking, funding support of up to 90% and project cost of more than $300,000 will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Economy, productivity, unemployment, wages
sections.summary: The economy has turned around, productivity has gone up, unemployment has gone down and wages are growing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The economy has turned around, productivity has gone up, unemployment rate has gone down and wages are growing.

sections.label: Job as best welfare
sections.summary: A job is the best welfare and full employment is the best protection for our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, we firmly believe that a job is the best welfare, and full employment is the best protection for our people.

sections.label: Technology, capability, staying ahead
sections.summary: Technology will destroy old jobs, but building new capability faster than competitors can make every enterprise, job and worker better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Advances in technology will destroy many old jobs globally and here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: But if we do more together to build new and better capability faster than our competitors, we can move ahead and stay ahead, to make every enterprise a better enterprise, every job a better job and every worker a better worker.

sections.label: Momentum since October 2015 launch
sections.summary: Since its October 2015 launch, about 6,700 companies have been helped, three times the number a year ago.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since its launch in October 2015, we have built up good momentum.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have helped about 6,700 companies, which are three times the number a year ago.

sections.label: Omoomodon salaries and manpower savings
sections.summary: Omoomodon offers salaries 15% above market rate, has lower attrition, and cut manpower per new outlet by up to 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Salaries offered by Omoomodon are, on average, 15% higher than market rate, there is lower attrition as workers are more motivated to stay.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Thanks to these measures, manpower required for each new outlet was reduced by up to 60%.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow placements 2017
sections.summary: The Adapt and Grow initiative placed more than 25,000 jobseekers in 2017, about 20% more than in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As mentioned by Minister Lim Swee Say, the Adapt and Grow initiative helped place more than 25,000 jobseekers into new jobs and careers in 2017, about 20% more than in 2016.

sections.label: MyCareersFuture portal launch timing
sections.summary: MyCareersFuture has run since 2 January this year and will be officially launched in the second quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MyCareersFuture has been up and running since 2 January this year and the portal will be officially launched in the second quarter this year.

sections.label: Mismatch case placements doubled
sections.summary: Placements of mismatch cases doubled from about 5,000 in 2016 to about 10,000 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Placements of mismatch cases doubled from about 5,000 in 2016 to about 10,000 in 2017.

sections.label: CSP wage support placements
sections.summary: Under enhanced CSP wage support, placements quadrupled from about 260 in 2016 to over 1,100 in 2017, over 80% long-term unemployed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With the enhanced wage support under CSP, placements have quadrupled from about 260 in 2016 to over 1,100 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Among the CSP placements, more than 80% were long-term unemployed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Within 12 months of placement, about 70% of those placed in 2015 and 2016 have remained in employment.

sections.label: Long-term unemployment rate for PMETs
sections.summary: The long-term unemployment rate for local PMETs improved from 0.9% in 2016 to 0.7% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, with a growing economy and these programmes in place, the long-term unemployment rate for local PMETs has improved from 0.9% in 2016 to 0.7% in 2017.

sections.label: Mature jobseekers helped through Adapt and Grow
sections.summary: Vincent is one of 13,000 mature jobseekers helped through Adapt and Grow in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Vincent is one of 13,000 mature jobseekers helped through Adapt and Grow in 2017.

sections.label: PCPs helping displaced and at-risk PMETs
sections.summary: About half are 50 and above, and over 100 PCPs in more than 30 sectors help displaced PMETs and those at risk of displacement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: About half of them, like Vincent, are 50 years old and above.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We now have over 100 PCPs in more than 30 sectors helping both displaced PMETs as well as those like Vincent who are at risk of displacement.

sections.label: Workers placed under such programmes
sections.summary: More than 2,000 workers were placed under such programmes in 2017, a more than 50% increase from 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: More than 2,000 workers were placed under such programmes in 2017, representing a more than 50% increase from 2016.

sections.label: Jobseekers placed through Work Trial
sections.summary: In 2017, jobseekers placed through Work Trial increased five times, from about 100 to 500.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2017, the number of jobseekers placed through Work Trial has increased five times, from about 100 to 500.

sections.label: Three new Attach-and-Train PCPs
sections.summary: Three new Attach-and-Train PCPs will be introduced by the second quarter of this year in AI Game Programmers, Robotics Engineers, and Food Production Specialists.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: First, we will introduce three new Attach-and-Train PCPs by the second quarter of this year in areas where we expect manpower demand to increase, namely, AI Game Programmers, Robotics Engineers, and Food Production Specialists.

sections.label: Enhanced Career Trial programme changes
sections.summary: The enhanced Career Trial doubles the maximum training allowance to $2,400 monthly and raises employer salary support to $5,400 per jobseeker over six months.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This was also a point which was raised by Mr Chong Kee Hiong.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will call the enhanced programme Career Trial.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under the Career Trial programme, we will double the maximum training allowance from $1,200 per month to $2,400 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Further, the salary support to employers and the Additional Retention Incentive, will be available for all jobseekers who are unemployed for six months or more, instead of only for those unemployed for 12 months or more previously.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will also increase the maximum salary support to employers, from $3,600 to $5,400 per jobseeker over a six-month period.

sections.label: Residents in self-employed work
sections.summary: A 2017 survey found 223,500 residents took up self-employed work for at least six months, about 10% more than the year before.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From our most recent survey in 2017, the number of residents who took up self-employed work for at least six months in 2017 has grown to 223,500, about 10% more than the year before.

sections.label: Government accepts seven recommendations
sections.summary: The Government accepts all seven recommendations and will find ways to fully implement them.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government accepts all seven recommendations and will find ways to fully implement them.

sections.label: Tripartite Standard on Contracting with SEPs
sections.summary: The Tripartite Standard on Contracting with SEPs was formally launched today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Some purchases are of very small value Instead, today, we formally launched the Tripartite Standard on Contracting with SEPs.

sections.label: Mediation for SEP payment disputes
sections.summary: With immediate effect, TADM will extend voluntary mediation services to all SEPs with payment disputes with businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With immediate effect, TADM will extend voluntary mediation services to all SEPs who have payment disputes with businesses.

sections.label: MOE contracting and PML insurance
sections.summary: MOE agreed in-principle to contract only with self-employed coaches and instructors having PML insurance coverage; taxi and private hire car drivers also benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MOE has agreed in-principle to help shape a new norm by contracting only with self-employed coaches and instructors who have such PML insurance coverage.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Another occupational group which will benefit from PML insurance are taxi drivers and private hire car drivers.

sections.label: PML insurance for drivers
sections.summary: MOM and LTA will study how to ensure active taxi and private hire car drivers have PML insurance coverage, with intermediaries and associations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MOM and LTA will study how to ensure that active taxi and private hire car drivers also have PML insurance coverage, together with these intermediaries, the National Taxi Association (NTA) and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association (NPHVA).

sections.label: PML insurance product 2019
sections.summary: The aim is a viable plan and a PML insurance product available in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The aim is to have a viable plan and for a PML insurance product to be available in 2019.

sections.label: CAYE model for SEPs
sections.summary: The Government agrees to study implementing the TWG's recommendation for a CAYE model for SEPs' MediSave contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It will be easier for them to make smaller, but more regular contributions as they receive the earnings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: So, this is why the Government agrees to study how to implement the TWG's recommendation for a CAYE model for SEPs' MediSave contributions.

sections.label: Government procurement CAYE pilot
sections.summary: Government Procurement Entities aim to start a pilot by 2020 to work through CAYE implementation issues and smoothen private sector implementation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Government Procurement Entities aim to start a pilot by 2020 which will allow us to work through the implementation issues for CAYE and help smoothen its subsequent implementation in the private sector.

sections.label: Priority sectors Skills Frameworks
sections.summary: To date, 15 of the 23 priority sectors have launched Skills Frameworks supporting the sector's industry transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To date, 15 of the 23 priority sectors have launched Skills Frameworks that support the sector's industry transformation.

sections.label: SEP recommendations implementation
sections.summary: Three recommendations are being implemented from today or ongoing, and another three will be implemented in 2019 or 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Three recommendations are being implemented from today or have been ongoing.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They are the Tripartite Standard on Contracting with SEPs, which we just launched; the extension of voluntary mediation services by TADM to cover SEPs; and the support of the tripartite partners for SEP associations to develop occupation-specific competency frameworks so that SEPs can remain relevant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Another three recommendations will be implemented in 2019 or 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They are to make available a PML insurance product.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To promote PML insurance coverage as a norm, starting with two occupational groups, namely, sports coaches and instructors, as well as taxi and private hire car drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: And to start a pilot programme where the Government, as a service buyer, will implement CAYE for the MediSave obligations for its self-employed contractors.

sections.label: Gender pay gap 2017
sections.summary: The data shows a gender pay gap of 11.8% in 2017 still exists.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The data shows that a gender pay gap of 11.8% in 2017 still exists.

sections.label: WorkPro Work-Life Grant funding
sections.summary: The Government will set aside about $30 million to promote FWAs through the enhanced WorkPro Work-Life Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Mr Desmond Choo and Ms Thanaletchimi will be pleased that during the event, I also announced that the Government will set aside about $30 million to further promote FWAs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will do so through the enhanced WorkPro Work-Life Grant, which will provide higher grant support to employers, especially for putting in place job-sharing schemes.

sections.label: CPF top-ups and transfers 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, over 61,000 members received about $1 billion in cash top-ups and over 35,000 received about $1 billion in CPF transfers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2017, over 61,000 members received about $1 billion in cash top-ups to their Special or Retirement Accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, over 35,000 members received about $1 billion in CPF transfers.

sections.label: Seniors qualifying for Silver Support
sections.summary: Today, about 152,000 seniors qualify for Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, about 152,000 seniors qualify for Silver Support.

sections.label: CPFIS-OA investment outcomes
sections.summary: Between October 2014 and September 2016, 29% of members who invested OA savings made cumulative total losses and 22% achieved profit at or below the 2.5% OA interest rate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over a two-year period between October 2014 and September 2016, 29% of members who invested their Ordinary Account (OA) savings made cumulative total losses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Another 22% achieved cumulative profit that is less than or just equal to the OA interest rate of 2.5% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In other words, slightly more than half of the members with a CPFIS-OA account did not do better through their own investments than if they simply left their CPF balances alone to earn a risk-free interest rate.

sections.label: CPFIS sales charges disallowed
sections.summary: The second enhancement is to disallow sales charges for products offered under the CPFIS.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The second enhancement is to disallow sales charges for products that are offered under the CPFIS.

sections.label: CPFIS wrap fee cap
sections.summary: The cap on annual wrap fees for CPFIS will be lowered to 0.4% of the total amount managed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Again, the targeted members for CPFIS are not expected to rely on advisory services that are usually included in the wrap fees.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, lower the cap on annual wrap fees to 0.4% of the total amount managed.

sections.label: CPFIS fee change timeline
sections.summary: Sales charge caps fall to 1.5% in October 2018 and 0% in October 2019, and wrap fee caps to 0.7% then 0.4%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Currently, the Life Insurance Association estimates that about 15% of premiums from new insurance business came from CPFIS products while the remaining 85% of premiums came from the cash market.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, to give the industry adequate time to adjust, we will implement these fee changes in two steps.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: (a) The cap on sales charges will be reduced to 1.5% from 1 October 2018 and further reduced to 0% from 1 October 2019; and (b) The cap on wrap fees for both existing and new accounts will be reduced from 1% to 0.7% from 1 October 2018 and further reduced to 0.4% from 1 October 2019.

sections.label: Lower investment scheme fees
sections.summary: Fees for various investment schemes will be lowered in future for members with time and investment knowledge.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For members with time and investment knowledge, fees charged for various investment schemes will be lowered in future.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We are taking active steps to help Singaporeans move into better jobs and secure better employment outcomes, even as the economy restructures.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The women in our workforce have made progress and will get more help to stay in employment.

sections.label: Older residents employment rate
sections.summary: The employment rate of residents aged 55 to 64 rose from 64% in 2012 to 67% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The employment rate of older residents aged 55 to 64 has increased from 64% in 2012 to 67% in 2017.

sections.label: Re-employment age raised
sections.summary: The re-employment age was raised from 65 to 67 in July 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: First, we raised the re-employment age from 65 to 67 in July 2017.

sections.label: Special Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: The Special Employment Credit scheme was extended, benefiting 93,000 employers and over 350,000 eligible older workers since 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Second, we extended the Special Employment Credit (SEC) scheme, which provides wage support to employers who hire older workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: So far, 93,000 employers who employed over 350,000 eligible older workers have benefited since SEC was extended in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: And since 2011, over $3 billion of SEC has been paid.

sections.label: WorkPro job redesign funding
sections.summary: WorkPro was enhanced in 2016 to provide funding of up to $300,000 per company to encourage job redesign adoption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: To encourage adoption of job redesign, we enhanced WorkPro in 2016 to provide more generous funding of up to $300,000 per company, and to complement other capability development grants.

sections.label: WIS and WTS payouts
sections.summary: Since 2007 WIS paid $5.5 billion to about 830,000 recipients, and since 2010 over 270,000 low-wage workers used WTS training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Since WIS started in 2007, a total of $5.5 billion has been paid to about 830,000 recipients, of which, $3.7 billion went to their CPF for their retirement; $1.8 billion was given to them in cash to supplement their income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Since 2010, more than 270,000 low-wage workers have tapped on WTS to upskill and reskill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: And more than $280 million was used to support such training efforts.

sections.label: PWM worker benefits
sections.summary: Over 70,000 resident workers have benefited from better wages and career progression through PWM.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Through PWM, over 70,000 resident workers have benefited from better wages and better career progression.

sections.label: Cleaners PWM wage increase
sections.summary: More than 41,000 cleaners can benefit from PWM basic wage increases of 3.4% to 4.6% per annum for six years from July 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: More than 41,000 cleaners can benefit from an increase in the PWM basic wages of between 3.4% and 4.6% per annum for six years, from July 2017 onwards.
