sections.label: Employment criteria for government contracts
sections.summary: NParks will add employment law criteria to the LCR, and from January 2019 Government procurement requires consistent employment and professional standards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Starting this year, NParks will introduce employment law criteria in the Landscape Company Register (LCR).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Going forward, employers in these three outsourced sectors stand to lose their eligibility to bid for Government contracts, if they contravene employment-related offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Additionally, from January 2019 onwards, the Government will only procure from companies with consistent track records in their employment and professional standards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We will require cleaning, security and landscape companies to have two consecutive accreditation status, good grading and LCR status respectively.

sections.label: KETs employment terms and salary
sections.summary: KETs state employment terms including working hours, leave benefits and salary, and employers cannot reduce IPA-stated salary without written consent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The KETs state clearly the employment terms, including working hours, leave benefits and the salary amount.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: It is an offence under our law for employers to reduce the salary from what is stated in the In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter without the worker’s written consent.

sections.label: WSH 2018 fatality rate target
sections.summary: A 2008 target aimed to cut the workplace fatality injury rate from 2.8 per 100,000 workers to 1.8 by 2018, and the rate fell to 1.2 last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Ten years ago, we set ourselves a "WSH 2018" target of reducing the workplace fatality injury rate from 2.8 per 100,000 workers in 2008 to 1.8 by 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Our workplace fatality rate dropped to 1.2 last year.

sections.label: New WSH2028 Tripartite Strategy Committee
sections.summary: A new WSH2028 Tripartite Strategy Committee will be convened, comprising industry, union and WSH leaders, chaired by Mr John Ng.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: To do this, I am pleased to announce that we will convene a new WSH2028 Tripartite Strategy Committee (WSH2028 Committee).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: This Committee will comprise leaders from industry, unions and key players in the WSH landscape and it will consult widely in the course of its work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: It will be chaired by Mr John Ng, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Singapore LNG Corporation, who is also a WSH Council member.

sections.label: WSH2028 Committee work timeline
sections.summary: The WSH2028 Committee will start work in April and intends to complete its report in a year's time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The WSH2028 Committee will start work in April and intends to complete its report in a year’s time.

sections.label: Foreign workers and South Korean model
sections.summary: One third, or 1.1 million, of workers are foreign workers, and the South Korean model is not thought adoptable in Singapore effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: One third, or 1.1 million, of our workers are foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: After very thorough studies, we do not think the South Korean model is something that can be adopted in Singapore effectively.

sections.label: Employment of Foreign Manpower Act
sections.summary: Singapore has put in place measures to protect foreign workers' interests and legislated the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act to protect their rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have put in place many measures to protect the interest of our foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: We have legislated an Act, the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act, to protect the rights of the foreign workers.

sections.label: Help from WSG and NTUC-e2i
sections.summary: Foreign workers do get help from WSG and NTUC-e2i, and 6,600 of them were helped last year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To Mr Low's question about whether they get help from WSG as well as NTUC-e2i, the answer is yes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I shared that, last year, we helped 6,600 of them.

sections.label: Freelancer career counselling advice
sections.summary: It is acceptable to freelance for extra income, and career counsellors and coaches should be equipped to advise on freelancing challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If they are doing it as a secondary form of employment, it is something that they decided to take on to earn an additional stream of income, we do not have any issues with that.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But we agree with the Member that it probably makes good sense to reach out to career counsellors, those who work with students, in particular, whether they are at the polytechnics or universities, or even other institutions, as well as our own career coaches, to help them appreciate what it is like to be a freelancer and the challenges that are faced, so that they can give correct advice.

sections.label: Dispute Resolution Centre scope expansion
sections.summary: A Member welcomes the one-stop Dispute Resolution Centre for salary claims and unfair dismissal and asks if it could later cover discrimination and harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: At the Second Reading of the Employment Claims Bill in August 2016, I suggested to the Ministry that we have one tribunal to handle salary claims, unfair dismissal as well as discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: So, I am happy to hear and I welcome the Minister's announcement that we are going to have a one-stop Dispute Resolution Centre to handle salary claims and unfair dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: My question to the Minister is: would the Minister consider, at some point in the future, to expand the service of this Dispute Resolution Centre to include claims and complaints relating to discrimination and workplace harassment?

sections.label: Percentage prepared to do so
sections.summary: The speaker recalls that at least more than 70% of them were prepared to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: As it turned out, the percentage was, if I recall correctly, at least more than 70% of them were prepared to do so.

sections.label: Salary and dismissal disputes transferred
sections.summary: All salary-related and wrongful dismissal disputes previously covered under the EA will now be transferred entirely to the ECT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: All salary-related and wrongful dismissal disputes, which were covered under the EA, will now be transferred to ECT entirely.

sections.label: Gender pay gap survey findings
sections.summary: Minister Josephine Teo shared the comprehensive Labour Force Survey on the gender pay gap, which still shows an 11.8% gap despite improvements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Minister Josephine Teo had shared with regard to the comprehensive Labour Force Survey that was done regarding the gender pay gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: It is troubling to hear that there is still an 11.8% gap, although there have been improvements.

sections.label: Female officers median pay higher
sections.summary: For a particular scheme of service, the median pay of female officers was higher than that of the males.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For a particular scheme of service, in fact, the median pay of the female officers was higher than the males.

sections.label: Gender pay gap plans
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether there are plans to address and further reduce the gender pay gap, especially in the private sector and senior management.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: It is heartening to know that, if you look at the public sector, the gap is probably not as much as 11.8% that the Minister shared earlier.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: But are there plans to address this gender pay gap and further reduce it, especially in the private sector and, especially those in senior management positions?

sections.label: Public sector superscale officers
sections.summary: The speaker says public sector data showed no difference between male and female superscale officers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I looked at the public sector data and it was quite interesting.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Certainly, among the superscale officers, there is no difference between the male and female officers.

sections.label: CTP private sector funding
sections.summary: For CTP, funding support is only for private sector organisations, not the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For CTP, funding support is only for the private sector organisations, not for public sector.

sections.label: Separate Tripartite Standard
sections.summary: The speaker says if there is good reason for a separate Tripartite Standard, they should look at it.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If there is a good reason for us to have a separate Tripartite Standard, yes, I think so, but let us take a look at it.

sections.label: Silver Support appeals
sections.summary: People can appeal on quantum or eligibility, both appeals are seriously looked into, and some cases were found worthy of higher Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the answer to the latter question is, yes, they can appeal for either the quantum or eligibility.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Both types of appeals are seriously looked into.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I accept the fact that, regardless of housing type, people can have complicated family arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There have been cases where we have reviewed and drawn the conclusion that they are worthy of higher support from the Silver Support.

sections.label: Maternity protection security
sections.summary: On Maternity Protection, the speaker says women should feel secure they can remain in work even when pregnant.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, to the question on Maternity Protection, our women should feel secure that they can remain in work even when they get pregnant.

sections.label: Singapore laws protect pregnant women
sections.summary: Singapore takes international conventions seriously and its laws already adequately protect pregnant women and those on Maternity Leave.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As a country that values very strongly our commitment whenever we sign on these international conventions, we do not take them lightly.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But let me assure the Member that the laws in Singapore already provide adequate protection to women who become pregnant, as well as when they are on Maternity Leave.
